correction.text: the Dominion of India with the North-East Frontier Tract (later the NEFA, now Arunachal Pradesh) except the Tawang tract: 'After the independence of India in 1947, NEFT became a part of the Assam state.' Sikkim is left out (a protectorate with its own dossier).

keyframe_review.note: 2.82 M km2 against the infobox's 3.29 M km2 (ratio 0.86): the infobox is today's area with the whole of Jammu and Kashmir, Hyderabad and the NEFA, none of which the 1947 shape holds, so the gap is expected. The shape is the Dominion of 15 August 1947 without Hyderabad and Kashmir (right: Kashmir acceded 26 October 1947, Hyderabad fell 13-18 September 1948; ledger). Three repairs. (1) 125 of the 310 Arunachal Pradesh cells are missing: Cliopatria drew them inside its Kingdom of Bhutan row until 1952 (the kingdom-of-bhutan dossier cuts that back), although the NEFA page says the frontier tract became part of Assam in 1947 and was renamed NEFA in 1951; they are added back. (2) Except the Tawang tract (15 cells, 12 of them inside Arunachal Pradesh, the cells Cliopatria's Tibet row holds and the tibet dossier keeps): the NEFA page does not mention Tawang; the Tawang page says that in February 1951 India 'took control of the remainder of the Tawang tract from the Tibetans, removing the Tibetan administration', and the Tawang district page that in 1944 'administrative control was extended over the area of the Tawang tract lying South of the Sela Pass' while 'no steps were taken to evict the Tibetan from the area North of the pass which contained Tawang town'. So the NEFA tracts south of the pass are Indian from 1947 and Tawang from February 1951 (ledger); the 15 cells sit around and north of Tawang town (27.5-28.2 N), and the grid cannot separate the strip south of the pass that Assam administered from 1944. (3) Sikkim (25 cells) is cut out: the Political integration page gives a 'full treaty with the Chogyal of Sikkim which in effect made it a protectorate' in 1950 and the Kingdom of Sikkim page 'Sikkim became an Indian protectorate in 1950' (no standstill agreement is named on either), while the kingdom-of-sikkim dossier draws the same land as its own to 1975; it is India's vassal from 1950 (ledger). The shape also holds the Daman and Diu cells, Portuguese until 1961 (Annexation of Goa page), which is below the grid's resolution.

keyframe_review.note: 3.13 M km2 for 1948-1952 as Cliopatria draws it. Adds Jammu and Kashmir (146 of 149 cells; India holds about two-thirds of the princely state after the 1947-48 war: Indo-Pakistani war page) and Hyderabad (Telangana 439 of 439 cells; Operation Polo, 13-18 September 1948: Political integration page), so the shape is the end-of-1948 state; the ledger carries the months. Three repairs. (1) NEFA as in 1947: Arunachal Pradesh is 187 of 310 cells here and the rest sits in Cliopatria's Bhutan shape until 1952; the Tawang tract is left out until February 1951 (see the 1947 keyframe and the new keyframe 1951). (2) Eastern Ladakh: 34 cells of Natural Earth's Ladakh (the Indian-administered part) lie outside Cliopatria's 1948 outline and outside Pakistan's 1948 shape (30 are still outside in 1962), and 27 of them are in its 1963 shape, 23 of them first drawn there (the other 4 enter in 1956 and 1961); the 1947-48 war page says India gained about two-thirds of the state, 'including the Kashmir Valley, the Jammu province and Ladakh', and that Pakistan held 'the Baltistan tehsil of the Ladakh district', so they are added back (the reviewer's option (a)). (3) Sikkim is cut out until the 1950 protectorate (see the 1947 keyframe); from 1950 it is a vassal (ledger) and the new keyframe 1951 and Cliopatria's later shapes hold it.

Sikkim is inside the shape again because it is India's protectorate from the 1950 treaty and Cliopatria's later shapes hold it (vassal tint, ledger). Source: Tawang page; the Ladakh and NEFA parts are as in the 1948 keyframe.

3.17 M km2 for 1953-1955. The 129 cells added in 1953 are the Arunachal Pradesh cells that Cliopatria's Bhutan row held until 1952 (114 cells) plus a few from its Tibet row (15); it is a repair of Cliopatria's own error, not an Indian gain. NEFA page: frontier tracts renamed the North-East Frontier Agency in 1951, divided into Kameng, Subansiri, Siang, Lohit and Tirap divisions in 1954. The French enclaves (1 November 1954) enter in the 1956 shape; the ledger carries them from 1954. Adjusted in the repair pass of 2026-10-25: the 1953 outline lacks 34 cells of Indian-administered Ladakh (outside Pakistan's 1948 shape) that India held from late 1947 and that Cliopatria draws, 27 of them by 1963; the 1947-48 war page (India gained 'Ladakh') is the source of the union, as in the 1948 keyframe.

keyframe_review.note: 3.18 M km2 for 1963-1972. The change from 1962 is 25 cells added and 4 removed along the Ladakh frontier (roughly 78-79 E, 32.5-35.3 N, partly in cells that Cliopatria's PRC shape also covers). 23 of the 25 added cells are Natural Earth's Ladakh and lie among the 34 cells that the 1948 keyframe (and 1953, 1956, 1961) now adds back, so this is Cliopatria repairing its own 1948-1962 outline, not an Indian gain or a new line. Sino-Indian War page: the infobox result is 'Status quo ante bellum', in the western theatre 'China already controlled most of the disputed territory' and 'Chinese forces quickly swept the region of any remaining Indian troops', and no Sino-Indian border change is dated 1963 (the only 1963 line on the page is the China-Pakistan border treaty). Left unexplained: 2 added cells (78.1 E 35.3 N and 79.0 E 33.4 N) and the 4 removed (78-79 E, 34.4-35.4 N), edge noise at the line. The shape stands.

3.18 M km2 for 1973-1975, 3.287 M km2 in the infobox (ratio 0.97; the infobox lists 'Territory claimed but not controlled'). Identical to the 1963 outline apart from 51 km2 of edge noise. Sikkim is inside the shape and is a protectorate until 1975 (vassal events); the 1975 event is in the ledger.
3.18 M km2 for 1976-1978; the same outline as 1963-1975 (the 51 km2 of 1973-1975 removed again). Sikkim a state from 1975 (ledger).

3.18 M km2 for 1979-1982: two cells at 91.0-91.7 E, 26.8 N (Assam-Bhutan border) added and one at 89.0 E removed against 1978; border noise on the Bhutan frontier, no event behind it on any page opened.
3.18 M km2 for 1983 (the shape runs to 1986): the 1979 border noise reverted. The Siachen Glacier region India took from April 1984 is not in this shape; see the new keyframe 1984.

ledger.note: 15 August 1947: the Dominion of India is born as British India is partitioned. 'Two new nations, Pakistan and India, came into existence on 14-15 August 1947' (infobox 'Dominion: 15 August 1947'). Manipur (11 August) and Tripura (13 August) had acceded in the days before (Political integration page); Hyderabad, Kashmir and Junagadh were still outside. The Tawang tract (Tibetan until February 1951) and Sikkim (a protectorate from 1950) are not part of the founding territory (repair pass of 2026-10-25).

ledger.note: 22-27 October 1947: the first Kashmir war begins. 'Following the accession of the state to India on 26 October 1947, Indian troops were airlifted to Srinagar, the state capital'; infobox dates the war '22 October 1947 - 1 January 1949'.

region.text: the part of the princely state India held: 'about two-thirds of the Jammu and Kashmir princely state', 'including the Kashmir Valley, the Jammu province and Ladakh'; without the Baltistan cells inside Pakistan's 1948 shape

ledger.note: 26 October 1947: Jammu and Kashmir accedes to India. The page does not draw the line; India 'gained control of about two-thirds of the Jammu and Kashmir princely state' (the Kashmir Valley, the Jammu province and Ladakh), and Pakistan held the western districts and 'the Baltistan tehsil of the Ladakh district' (later Gilgit-Baltistan), so the Indian-held part is taken here as NE's Jammu and Kashmir plus Ladakh minus Pakistan's 1948 shape (368 cells; 34 of them, all in Ladakh, lie outside Cliopatria's 1948 outline, which is why the 1948, 1953, 1956 and 1961 keyframes add them back). Repaired 2026-10-25: the region no longer holds the cells inside Pakistan's 1948 shape.

region.text: Junagadh state in Saurashtra

ledger.note: November 1947: India takes over Junagadh. The page (paraphrased): the Nawab chose to accede to Pakistan and fled there on 26 October after clashes with Indian troops; on 7 November the court invited the Government of India to take over administration and India agreed; a plebiscite in February 1948 went 'almost unanimously in favour of accession to India'. The page gives the days, not the year (inferred from the February 1948 plebiscite). Cliopatria's 1947 shape already holds these cells; Pakistan 'claims sovereignty over Junagadh state' to this day (page).

region.text: the Nizam's dominions, 82,000 square miles on the page

ledger.note: 13-18 September 1948: Operation Polo ends the Nizam's rule. On 13 September 1948 'the Indian Army was sent into Hyderabad under Operation Polo' and Indian troops took complete control between 13 and 18 September 1948 (paraphrased); the page puts the state at 'over 212,000 square kilometres'.

region.text: the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir

ledger.note: 1 January 1949: the UN-mediated ceasefire ends the Kashmir war. 'At 23.59 hrs on 1 January 1949, a United Nations-mediated ceasefire came into effect'; India and Pakistan 'signed the Karachi Agreement in July 1949 and established a ceasefire line'. India keeps 'about two-thirds' of the state.

region.text: the 83 km2 of territory of Dewangiri in southeastern Bhutan

ledger.note: August 1949: India returns Dewangiri to Bhutan with the Treaty of Friendship. History of Bhutan: 'on August 8, 1949, Thimphu signed the Treaty of Friendship Between the Government of India and the Government of Bhutan' and 'Important to Bhutan's national pride was the return of Dewangiri'. The page gives no date for the transfer itself, does not name the returning party in so many words and gives no area; the 83 km2 is the figure of the Duar War passage cited by the kingdom-of-bhutan dossier (ledger 18 and 20), which this event mirrors. Under one grid cell. Added in the repair pass of 2026-10-25.

region.text: Sikkim

ledger.note: 1950: Sikkim becomes an Indian protectorate. Political integration page (paraphrased): a 1950 treaty with the Chogyal 'in effect made it a protectorate'; Kingdom of Sikkim page: 'Sikkim became an Indian protectorate in 1950'. Neither gives a month or names an earlier standstill arrangement, so the corrected 1947 and 1948 keyframes leave Sikkim out of India's shape (it is kingdom-of-sikkim's own land until the treaty) and the tint starts here; Cliopatria's later shapes hold Sikkim as part of India. The kingdom-of-sikkim dossier has no matching vassal_start (route to its owner).

26 January 1950: the Dominion becomes the Republic of India. Infobox 'Republic: 26 January 1950'; 'The Constitution of India was adopted in 1950 and declared India to be a federal republic.' The state, colour and territory continue.

region.text: Chandernagore (Chandannagar), a French enclave on the Hooghly

ledger.note: 2 May 1950: Chandernagore passes from France to India. The Political integration page does name it: after the plebiscite of 19 June 1949 (7,463 to 114 for India) 'It was ceded to India on a de facto basis on 14 August 1949 and de jure on 2 May 1950.' The sibling french-india dossier (Chandannagar page) dates the de facto transfer to 2 May 1950, so the pages disagree on the de facto date; May 1950 is kept to match the sibling, confidence 2. Cliopatria adds the West Bengal cell only in 1956. (Confidence and note corrected by reviewer sa-06-e, 2026-10-25.)

region.text: the Tawang tract, taken from Tibet in February 1951: India 'took control of the remainder of the Tawang tract from the Tibetans, removing the Tibetan administration' (Tawang page, as the fetch tool returned it); the same 15 cells (Cliopatria's Tibet row of 1939 minus its row of 1938) that the tibet dossier uses for the tract

ledger.note: February 1951: India takes the Tawang tract from Tibet. Tawang page (as the fetch tool returned it): 'In February 1951, India sent an official with a small escort and several hundred porters to Tawang' and 'took control of the remainder of the Tawang tract from the Tibetans, removing the Tibetan administration'; the day is not given. Tawang district page: in 1944 'administrative control was extended over the area of the Tawang tract lying South of the Sela Pass', but 'no steps were taken to evict the Tibetan from the area North of the pass which contained Tawang town'. The tract is the 15-cell spec the tibet dossier uses (its ledger 39-41 hold it for Tibet from 1947, confidence 1); India's 1947 and 1948 corrections leave it out, so this gain is its first entry into India's shape. The tibet owner (ea-06) should add the mirror loss of 1951-2. Added in the repair pass of 2026-10-25.

region.text: the French establishments of Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam

ledger.note: 1 November 1954: Pondicherry passes to India. The page (paraphrased): a referendum in October 1954 favoured merger and de facto control passed on 1 November 1954. The page names Pondicherry only; Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam, the other French establishments, are taken with it (french-india dossier), which is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Dadra and Nagar Haveli

ledger.note: 1961: Dadra and Nagar Haveli become a Union Territory of India. The page (paraphrased): an uprising in July 1954 threw off Portuguese rule and the area became a Union Territory in 1961. Annexation of Goa page: armed activists forced the Portuguese forces to surrender between 22 July and 2 August 1954 and Nagar Haveli's administrator and police surrendered on 11 August 1954. Portugal recognised Indian sovereignty only in the treaty of 31 December 1974.

ledger.note: 17 December 1961: Operation Vijay begins. Hostilities began at 09:45 on 17 December 1961 near Maulinguem and the main ground assault came on 18 December (paraphrased; infobox '17-19 December 1961').

region.text: Goa, Daman and Diu, about 1,540 square miles (4,000 km2) in total on the page

ledger.note: 19 December 1961: Portugal surrenders Goa. The Portuguese governor general Manuel Antonio Vassalo e Silva signed the instrument of surrender at 20:30 on 19 December.

region.text: Goa, Daman and Diu, about 1,540 square miles (4,000 km2) in total on the page

ledger.note: December 1961: Goa, Daman and Diu join India. Goa, Daman and Diu was declared a federally administered union territory in December 1961 (paraphrased); Operation Vijay 17-19 December 1961, infobox result 'Indian victory'.

ledger.note: 21 November 1962: the guns fall silent. 'Beginning from 21 November 1962, the Chinese frontier guards will cease fire along the entire Sino-Indian border'; the infobox territorial result is 'Status quo ante bellum', China withdrawing (paraphrased) to its pre-war position, the effective border also known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

region.text: the sectors where ground changed hands: Haji Pir, Chhamb, Khem Karan, Sialkot, Lahore and the high ground over Kargil

ledger.note: 5 August 1965: Pakistani infiltrators cross the Line of Control in Kashmir. 'On 5 August 1965, Pakistani soldiers crossed the Line of Control dressed as Kashmiri locals'; Pakistan 'occupied high ground overlooking Kargil and Srinagar-Leh road' until forced out in August, and Indian forces 'captured the Haji Pir pass, 8 km into Pakistan administered Kashmir by 28 August'. The page names the sectors, not their outline: the zone is a circle round each (Haji Pir, Chhamb, Khem Karan, Sialkot, Lahore, the Kargil heights), the researcher's reading.

region.text: the sectors where ground changed hands: Haji Pir, Chhamb, Khem Karan, Sialkot, Lahore and the high ground over Kargil

ledger.note: 10 January 1966: the Tashkent Declaration. The fighting ended with Pakistan's acceptance of the ceasefire on 23 September 1965 (the UN Security Council resolution is dated 20 September), but ground stayed in the other side's hands until the declaration, 'agreeing to withdraw to pre-August lines no later than 25 February 1966'. India gained 460 km2 in the Sialkot sector and 360 km2 on the Lahore front, Pakistan 490 km2 in the Chhamb sector and 50 km2 around Khem Karan (page, from Van Praagh); all of it went back, so no gain or loss is recorded.

region.text: the 780 km2 of the Rann of Kutch awarded to Pakistan: the page names no outline, so the circle (about 800 km2) is the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1968: the Kutch tribunal awards part of the Rann to Pakistan. 'The verdict which came later in 1968, saw Pakistan awarded 780 square kilometres (301 square miles)' of Pakistan's claimed 9,100 km2 (the page gives the year only, no day or month, and does not say whether or when the land was handed over; the reviewer's 1969 handover is not on the page, and 'about 900 km2' is not the page's figure). June 1965: Harold Wilson persuaded both countries to end the hostilities and they agreed to international arbitration. The Rann of Kutch page, opened for the date, does not mention the dispute. About 3 grid cells; mirror gain in islamic-republic-of-pakistan (route to sa-06).

region.text: East Pakistan

ledger.note: 3 December 1971: India enters the war in East Pakistan. 'India joined the war on 3 December 1971 in support of the Mukti Bahini.' The Pakistani air strikes of the same day 'marked the official start of the Indo-Pakistani War'.

region.text: East Pakistan

ledger.note: 16 December 1971: Pakistan surrenders in Dhaka. 'Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971'; East Pakistan became the People's Republic of Bangladesh and India annexed nothing there.

region.text: Kachchatheevu, a small island in Palk Strait

ledger.note: 1974: Kachchatheevu passes to Sri Lanka. 'In 1974, Kachchatheevu, a small island in Palk Strait, was formally ceded to Sri Lanka', linked on the page to the 'Sirima-Gandhi Pact of 1974'. Under one grid cell; the page does not name India as the ceding party in so many words.

Kingdom of Sikkim page: 'Sikkim's merger with India is dated 16 May 1975' (lead: '16 May 1975, when it was annexed by India'). Political integration page (paraphrased): on 10 April 1975 the assembly passed a resolution calling for full integration and a referendum on 14 April 1975 was endorsed by 97 percent. The corrected 1947-1949 shapes leave Sikkim out, Cliopatria's shapes hold it as a vassal inside India from 1950, so from 1975 the cells do not change. Month added in the repair pass of 2026-10-25.

region.text: the Siachen Glacier region

ledger.note: 3 May 1999: shepherds report a Pakistani intrusion in the Kargil district. 'The total area seized by the ingress is generally accepted to between 130 and 200 km2'; the intrusions were in 'the heights of the lower Mushkoh Valley', along the Marpo La ridgeline in Drass, in Kaksar near Kargil, in the Batalik sector and in the Turtuk sector. The page gives no outline: the zone is a circle round Kargil and one round Turtuk, the researcher's reading. Added in the repair pass of 2026-10-25.

wars.note: Mirpur fell to tribal forces on 25 November 1947; the brigade linked up at Kargil on 24 November; Skardu surrendered on 14 August (year not on the page).

wars.name: Operation Polo
wars.outcome: Indian troops took complete control between 13 and 18 September 1948 (paraphrased); Hyderabad ceased to be a state.
wars.note: Nehru's ultimatum 7 September 1948; the page gives no accession date.

wars.name: Annexation of Goa

zones.text: Goa, Daman and Diu, about 1,540 square miles (4,000 km2) in total on the page

wars.outcome: Indian victory in two days; Goa, Daman and Diu became a union territory in December 1961. Portugal recognised Indian sovereignty by treaty on 31 December 1974.

wars.name: Sino-Indian War

zones.text: the Tawang Tract and Aksai Chin

wars.outcome: Chinese victory; 'Status quo ante bellum' on the page's infobox, China withdrawing to the Line of Actual Control.
wars.note: 20 October to 21 November 1962 (the page disagrees with itself on 20 or 21 November for the ceasefire).

wars.name: Indo-Pakistani war of 1965

zones.text: the sectors where ground changed hands: Haji Pir, Chhamb, Khem Karan, Sialkot, Lahore and the high ground over Kargil

wars.outcome: Stalemate with the ground returned: Pakistan accepted the ceasefire on 23 September 1965 (UN resolution 20 September); the Tashkent Declaration of 10 January 1966 agreed to withdraw 'to pre-August lines no later than 25 February 1966'. India took Haji Pir and 460 km2 in the Sialkot sector and 360 km2 on the Lahore front, Pakistan 490 km2 in the Chhamb sector and 50 km2 around Khem Karan (page). The Rann of Kutch tribunal of 1968 awarded Pakistan 780 km2 (ledger).
wars.note: Opened in the repair pass of 2026-10-25. 'On 5 August 1965, Pakistani soldiers crossed the Line of Control dressed as Kashmiri locals'; infobox '5 August - 23 September 1965'. The zones are circles round the named sectors (the page gives no outline).

wars.name: Bangladesh Liberation War
wars.outcome: 'Bangladeshi-Indian victory': Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 and East Pakistan became Bangladesh; India annexed no land.
wars.note: India's war with Pakistan is 3-16 December 1971 (3 December strikes; surrender 16 December). The western front is not on the page and its border effects are unverified.

wars.name: Siachen conflict
wars.outcome: Indian victory: India holds the Saltoro Ridge heights (about 2,500 km2); ceasefire 25 November 2003.

wars.name: Kargil War

zones.text: the Kargil district sectors where Pakistani forces held the heights: Dras, Kaksar, Batalik and Turtuk; 'between 130 and 200 km2' on the page, far less than the circles

wars.outcome: Indian victory on the infobox, territorial result 'Status quo ante bellum': Pakistani forces held 130-200 km2 of heights in the Kargil district from May until the fighting ceased on 26 July 1999.
wars.note: Opened in the repair pass of 2026-10-25. Intrusion reported 3 May 1999 by local shepherds; the zone is a circle round Kargil and one round Turtuk (the page gives no outline).

certainty.note: The princely states are acceding or being absorbed, the Kashmir front moves until the ceasefire of 1 January 1949, and the Hyderabad border is that of the Nizam's dominions; only the Radcliffe Line frontiers (Bengal, Punjab) are fixed.

Treaty and survey frontiers with Pakistan (Radcliffe Line, 1947), Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar. The exceptions are soft: the Kashmir ceasefire line (Karachi Agreement, July 1949) and Line of Control, the Siachen Actual Ground Position Line (1984-), and the frontier with China (McMahon Line in the east, Line of Actual Control in Ladakh and Aksai Chin).

notes:
Written by sa-06-e on 2026-10-25. Pages: nine are listed, seven opened for India (India, Political integration, Sino-Indian War, North-East Frontier Agency [read twice], Indo-Pakistani war of 1947-1948, Siachen conflict, Annexation of Goa) against a budget of five, because the 1984 Siachen shape, the Goa shape and the Kashmir war could not otherwise be dated; the Bangladesh Liberation War and Sri Lanka pages were opened for the other two dossiers of this batch and are cited here for the 1971 contest and Kachchatheevu.
Repair pass of 2026-10-25 (reviewer finding: fail on the Tawang tract). Seven more pages opened: Tawang, Tawang district, Kingdom of Sikkim, History of Bhutan, Indo-Pakistani war of 1965, Kargil War, Rann of Kutch (the last has nothing on the dispute); the Indo-Pakistani war of 1947-1948 and Sino-Indian War pages were read again. 16 pages in all against a budget of 5.
(1) CLIOPATRIA ERRORS. (a) 1947-1952 shapes lack the NEFA (Arunachal Pradesh): Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bhutan row holds about 114 of its cells until 1952 (the kingdom-of-bhutan dossier repairs that) and its Tibet row 15; repaired by union with Arunachal Pradesh (adjust, 1947 and 1948) EXCEPT the Tawang tract (15 cells, 12 inside Arunachal Pradesh), which Tibet administered until February 1951 (Tawang page) and India gains in the ledger; a new keyframe 1951-1952 holds it. The tibet dossier (ea-06) keeps the tract from 1947 and needs the mirror loss of 1951-2. The tract spec includes the strip south of the Sela Pass that Assam administered from 1944 (Tawang district page); the 15-cell spec cannot separate it and is the one the tibet dossier uses. (b) Sikkim: the corrected 1947 and 1948 shapes leave it out (25 cells), because neither the Political integration page nor the Kingdom of Sikkim page names any relation to India before the 1950 protectorate and kingdom-of-sikkim draws the land as its own; from 1950 it is a vassal inside India's shape (Cliopatria's 1953-2024 shapes hold it) and the vassal events tint it to the merger of 16 May 1975. In 1950 itself the 1948 keyframe omits it and the tint stands in. (c) The 1947 shape holds the Daman and Diu cells (Portuguese to December 1961) and 4 Goa cells, below the grid's resolution; left as they are. (d) Two sliver polygons at 63.8 E 29.5 N and 66.3 E 29.95 N in the raw 1948-1978 geometry produce no land cell; ignore. (e) Shapes overlap neighbours by a few border cells (Pakistan 9, Bangladesh 13, Nepal 15, Myanmar 17, China 12-23): grid tolerance. (f) Eastern Ladakh: Cliopatria's 1948 outline lacks 34 cells of Indian-administered Ladakh (outside Pakistan's 1948 shape), 27 of which it draws by 1963 (23 first in 1963); added back to the 1948, 1953, 1956 and 1961 keyframes (the reviewer's option (a)), so the 1963 redraw is Cliopatria repairing itself and needs no event (23 of its 25 added cells); 2 added and 4 removed cells at the line stay unexplained; 1979-1982: 3 border cells on the Bhutan frontier: noise, no page opened explains them (the Bhutan-India border page was not opened; the reviewer accepted this within the budget).
(2) EVENTS. Added in the repair pass: India's loss of Dewangiri to Bhutan (August 1949, mirror of kingdom-of-bhutan ledger 20, confidence 2: the page dates the treaty, not the transfer, and does not name India as the returning party); the 1965 war (contest 5 August 1965 to the Tashkent Declaration of 10 January 1966, six circular zones) and the Rann of Kutch award of 1968 (loss, 780 km2 on the page; the reviewer's 'about 900 km2' and 1969 handover are not on the page); the Kargil War (contest 3 May to 26 July 1999, two circles). Still not recorded: the merger of Manipur and Tripura (October 1949; carried by those dossiers' dissolve events), the 2015 enclave exchange, the western front of 1971 (Chhamb and the other lands returned after the Simla Agreement). kingdom-of-sikkim dates its end May 1975; this ledger now gives 16 May 1975 from the Kingdom of Sikkim page.
(3) CONFIDENCE 1: none left (Chandernagore raised to 2 by the reviewer: Political integration page, de facto 14 August 1949 and de jure 2 May 1950; the sibling french-india dossier has 2 May 1950, so the pages disagree and May 1950 is kept). Confidence 2: Junagadh (year inferred), Pondicherry enclaves, the Kashmir gain region, the Tawang/Aksai Chin zones, Kachchatheevu, Siachen, Dewangiri, the 1965 and Kargil zones, the Rann award.
(4) COUNTERPART SLUGS. The kashmir-and-jammu dossier lists republic-of-india as a successor but has no loss event to India; this ledger's gain of October 1947 is its counterpart (route to sa-06). tibet (ea-06) needs the 1951-2 loss; kingdom-of-sikkim needs the 1950 vassal_start with India; islamic-republic-of-pakistan (sa-06) needs the 1984-4 Siachen loss, the 1965 and Kargil zones and contest events, and the 1968 Rann gain; kingdom-of-bhutan, hyderabad-state, french-india, portuguese-india, sri-lanka, people-s-republic-of-china have or will have dossiers. 'junagadh-state' and 'Free Dadra and Nagar Haveli' have none.
(5) GAZETTEER. Names the gazetteer lacks: Aksai Chin as a region (110 km radius at 79.3 E 35.2 N); the Tawang Tract (91.86 E 27.59 N, 70 km); Junagadh as a place (70.46 E 21.52 N, 50 km); Kachchatheevu (79.52 E 9.38 N; a 5 km radius holds no land cell); Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam, Chandernagore; Dewangiri (the Bhutan dossier's spelling, resolves to no place); Haji Pir, Chhamb, Khem Karan, Kargil, Turtuk and the Great Rann of Kutch (circles by coordinates here).
(6) NEFA. The NEFA page says the NEFT 'became a part of the Assam state' after 1947 but does not mention Tawang, the Tawang Tract or the McMahon Line (the reviewer confirmed); the 1962 war page says China captured the Tawang Tract in October 1962 and withdrew to the pre-war line.
(7) PRINCELY STATES. After the Instruments of Accession the princely states are treated as India's land without a vassal tint (Sikkim excepted); the integration page dates Saurashtra (January 1948), Madhya Bharat (28 May 1948), PEPSU (15 July 1948), Rajasthan (15 May 1949) and Travancore-Cochin (mid-1949) as unions of states, not as territory changes.
